title: An agent is LLMs using tools in a loop on environmental feedback - design the tools accordingly
statement: Treat an agent as an LLM calling tools in a loop against environmental feedback, and invest in the agent-computer interface (clear tool docs, unambiguous parameters, poka-yoke arguments) as heavily as the prompt itself.
rationale: Because the loop is just tool call then observe, tool quality bounds agent quality. Ambiguous or error-prone tools produce compounding mistakes that no amount of prompt tuning fixes.
applies_when: The agent has more than a couple of tools
not_when: A pure single-shot generation task with no tools
how: Write each tool's description like a docstring for a junior developer, with example usage and edge cases
Remove tools with overlapping purpose; if a human cannot say which tool applies, neither can the model
Change arguments so mistakes are hard to make (e.g. require absolute paths, not relative)
check: For each tool, can a new engineer say from the description alone exactly when to use it and not confuse it with another? If not, the tool set is a failure source.
failure_if_absent: The agent picks the wrong tool, mis-formats arguments, and accumulates errors that look like model weakness but are interface weakness.

evidence.title: Anthropic - Building Effective Agents
evidence.quote: They are typically just LLMs using tools based on environmental feedback in a loop. It is therefore crucial to design toolsets and their documentation clearly and thoughtfully
evidence.note: The appendix reports they spent more time optimizing tools than the overall prompt on SWE-bench.
